input.question: Which award did Eugene I. Shakhnovich receive?

documents.text:
Here is a Wikipedia-style entry that presents comprehensive evidence for the statement:

Eugene I. Shakhnovich

Eugene I. Shakhnovich is a Soviet and American biophysicist who has made significant contributions to the field of biophysics. Early Life and Education

Shakhnovich was born in the Soviet Union and received his undergraduate degree in physics from Moscow State University. He later earned his Ph.D. in biophysics from the same institution. Career

Shakhnovich's research focuses on the application of physical principles to understand biological systems. He has held faculty positions at several prestigious institutions, including Harvard University and the University of California, San Diego. Awards and Honors

Shakhnovich has received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to biophysics. One of his notable awards is the Packard Fellowship for Science and Engineering. Packard Fellowship for Science and Engineering

The Packard Fellowship for Science and Engineering is a prestigious award that recognizes early-career scientists and engineers who have demonstrated exceptional promise in their field. The fellowship is awarded annually by the David and Lucile Packard Foundation to support innovative research in the fields of science and engineering. Evidence of Award

According to the David and Lucile Packard Foundation's website, Eugene I. Shakhnovich was awarded the Packard Fellowship for Science and Engineering in 1996. [1] This award is a testament to Shakhnovich's outstanding contributions to the field of biophysics and his potential for future innovation. References:

[1] David and Lucile Packard Foundation. (n.d.). Packard Fellows.
